newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end down in low volume, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end down in low volume, profit-taking.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed lower on Friday in apathetic trading that saw the week's trend of profit-taking continue, brokers said.
They added that the market was close to the bottom and probably would rise again early next week.
The General Index .IGRA fell 0.58 percent to 1,555.82 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL fell 0.68 percent to 2,077.7, according to preliminary stock figures.
In 2,071 operations, 16 shares rose, 30 fell and 42 were unchanged on low volume of 30.4 million sols ($12.0 million).
This week's profit-taking has completely cancelled out the previous week's large rises, brokers said.
The biggest losers were the stocks that had risen most sharply, particularly the two sister breweries Compania Nacional de Cerveza (CNC) and Backus y Johnston .
CNC dropped 2.22 percent to 1.32 soles on 348,000 shares, while Backus -- the country's largest brewery -- dropped 3.28 percent to 2.65 soles on 750,000 shares.
"In general it was a profit-taking day. In some cases it seems there was a little fear and investors sold stocks," said Lorenzo Wong of local brokerage Intercapital.
He added that uncertainty over whether or not Backus and CNC would fuse -- as company officials said was being mused -- had made players cautious about keeping hold of the stocks.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru continued to outperform the market as it remained stable at 5.73 soles on volume of 1.4 million shares.
